title: Buyer pays $350 for broken RTX 4090 project only to find realistic fake GPU die and swapped memory
content: A customer paid approximately $350 for what appeared to be a repairable RTX 4090, only to receive a fake GPU with components that were painstakingly designed to resemble the real thing.

title: Interview: Microsoft's Maia GM on Maia 300, Taiwan and HBM supply
content: Microsoft's in-house Azure Maia chips will become the main platform for its own AI services, including Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry. However, the company will keep using GPUs from Nvidia and AMD, Andrew Wall, general manager of the Azure Maia program, told DIGITIMES.

title: Microsoft's Maia 300 rack: 96 accelerators, HBM4, mostly liquid-cooled
content: Microsoft has released architecture details for Maia 300, its third-generation Azure AI accelerator. The design pairs 96 accelerators per rack with a two-tier network that links up to 12,288 accelerators into a single superpod. The company says the system is built for cloud-scale agentic inference, and that it co-designed the software, silicon, rack infrastructure, networking, and data centers to run as one platform.

title: Microsoft to scale Maia AI chips to multi-gigawatt deployments, unveils TSMC N2P-based Maia 300
content: Microsoft will scale its in-house Azure Maia AI accelerators to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, making Maia the primary AI inference system for its products and services. The company also unveiled Maia 300, the third generation of the chip family, which it says will start production deployments next year.

title: <sub></sub>Apple iPhone launch and holiday demand lift Momo revenue to a record September
content: Fubon Multimedia, which operates the Momo e-commerce platform, reported consolidated revenue of approximately NT$8.59 billion (US$269.4 million) in September 2026, up 8.2% from a year earlier. Revenue for the first nine months reached nearly NT$80 billion, an increase of about 3.9%, setting records for the period on both a monthly and cumulative basis.

title: HHGalaxy reports record 3Q26 revenue as Double 11 demand builds
content: Taiwanese e-commerce operations provider HHGalaxy reported consolidated revenue of NT$621 million (US$19.5 million) for September 2026, up 31.74% from a year earlier, as brands prepared for the Single's Day shopping event. Revenue for the first nine months reached NT$4.925 billion, a 26.76% annual increase, while third-quarter revenue rose 34.43% to NT$1.774 billion, setting a third-quarter record.

title: Chinese government and industry make full push into AI glasses development: AR display integration and lightweighting gain traction
content: DIGITIMES notes that China continued to advance smart glasses policies from the central government to local governments in 2026, driving both enterprise production and consumer purchase subsidies.

title: Finland orders Google to halt work at two AI data center sites
content: Finnish authorities ordered Google to suspend parts of construction at planned AI data centers in Muhos and Kajaani after forests were allegedly cleared at the sites before an environmental impact assessment was completed. The decision affects Google subsidiary Tuike Finland Oy and introduces uncertainty around the company's US$15 billion investment plan in Finland.

title: EU caps annual HEV imports at 350,000 to curb trade deficit with China
content: The European Union plans to cap imports of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) at 350,000 units per year, with safeguard measures potentially taking effect as early as December 1, 2026. The four-year framework sets a 350,000-unit limit in its first year, followed by a 6% annual quota expansion starting in the second year, while both sides commit to complying with World Trade Organization (WTO) rules.

title: Samsung reportedly secures long-term contracts covering up to 80% of 2027 memory supply
content: Samsung Electronics has committed 75–80% of its 2027 memory supply, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM), to long-term agreements (LTAs), the Korea Economic Daily reported on October 9, 2026, citing industry sources. Nvidia, Google and Microsoft were among the major customers that had largely finalized contracts. Samsung has not confirmed the allocation or named the buyers.

title: Nanya gross margin hits 85.7% as low-priced DRAM contracts roll off
content: Nanya Technology reported record quarterly earnings in the third quarter of 2026, according to unaudited results released on October 12, as DRAM average selling prices (ASPs) rose more than 60% sequentially following the expiration of low-priced long-term agreements (LTAs).

title: Memory surge lifts phone prices, boosting N-1 and used-device demand
content: Rising memory prices have forced smartphone brands to raise handset prices, hurting new-device sales in 2026. Global smartphone shipments are expected to drop 15-17%, while demand for N-1 generation and used smartphones is surging, potentially pushing the used-phone market beyond 300 million units and creating new orders for display, battery, and casing suppliers.

title: How 'Filter Moore's Law' is doubling revenue for a Taiwan chip filter maker
content: Under what the industry terms the "Filter Moore's Law," each process node shrink lowers tolerance for airborne molecular contaminants, causing filtration demand to grow exponentially. For global airborne molecular contamination (AMC) filtration leader Ye Siang Enterprise, that demand is now showing up in record revenue.

title: Chenbro Micom expands into Nvidia Vera Rubin rack-scale systems, 2026 revenue already tops full-year 2025
content: Taiwanese server chassis maker Chenbro Micom is expanding its role in AI infrastructure, moving beyond traditional server enclosures into high-end AI servers and rack-level solutions. The company has secured involvement in multiple Nvidia Vera Rubin platform projects covering GPUs, CPUs, and storage, while custom ASIC programs for cloud service providers (CSPs) are gradually scaling up according to schedule.

title: Largan signals early peak-season cut, challenging phone chips in 4Q26
content: Largan chairman and CEO Adam Lin said October 2026 orders are tracking at roughly the same level as September's, but will begin declining in November as customers cut their forecasts after new phones went on sale. The comments signal that demand across the smartphone supply chain will weaken in the fourth quarter of 2026, creating challenges for handset chipmakers and other suppliers that performed strongly during the third quarter.

title: Moonshot AI's Hong Kong IPO faces a critical ownership dispute ahead of US$50 billion debut
content: China's Moonshot AI is seeking to settle a shareholder dispute involving claims potentially exceeding US$700 million ahead of a potential US$5 billion Hong Kong initial public offering (IPO). Allegations concerning asset transfers and corporate governance could complicate the AI startup's listing preparations.

title: South Korea's Nucode targets US drone identification market with Realtek-based module
content: South Korean wireless communications module maker Nucode has signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with US drone identification and airspace intelligence provider Zing Drone Solutions to develop and supply electronic component modules for ultra-small and small-scale solutions. Nucode's NU87 module, which uses a Realtek chip, is among the products submitted for evaluation.

title: Biren's BR20X GPU targets 1,024-chip AI systems, but US curbs cloud mass production
content: China's Biren Technology has successfully powered on its next-generation BR20X GPU, advancing to post-tapeout validation while preparing for customer sampling and mass production. The milestone advances its AI accelerator roadmap, though US export controls and manufacturing constraints remain major obstacles.
